The best universities in the Midwest include the University of Chicago, Northwestern, Washington University in St. Louis, Notre Dame and the University of Michigan. For engineering and computer science, add Illinois Urbana-Champaign and Purdue. For a smaller undergraduate community, consider Carleton or Grinnell.

Your subject should shape the shortlist. So should your budget. An economics applicant and a mechanical engineering applicant need different curricula, admission routes and financial options.

This guide compares 25 Midwest universities and colleges, explains their differences and gives published cost and scholarship examples for students planning a 2027 start.

How We Selected These Midwest Universities and Colleges

This guide uses the Census Bureau's regional boundaries: 12 states across the East North Central and West North Central divisions.

The selection balances undergraduate subject choice, institution type, learning environment and practical affordability. It includes research universities and liberal arts colleges because both can suit a student seeking a bachelor's degree, although they offer different experiences.

Leading Midwest Universities and Colleges in Detail

University of Chicago

Chicago suits students who enjoy analytical reading, discussion and quantitative thinking. Economics, mathematics and the social sciences provide useful starting points, but the undergraduate experience extends beyond a single major.

Its shared Core curriculum asks students to study across disciplines. Choose it if broad intellectual training appeals to you; compare other curricula if you want fewer compulsory subjects.

Northwestern University

Northwestern combines an Evanston campus with access to the Chicago area. Its undergraduate schools cover fields including journalism, engineering, communication and music, making it worth considering when your interests cross professional and academic subjects.

Washington University in St. Louis

WashU offers routes through arts and sciences, business, engineering, architecture and art. Its undergraduate academic options include a joint business and computer science degree, alongside pre-health advising for students pursuing different majors.

Consider it for combined business and technology interests or preparation for health-profession study. Pre-med advising does not secure a medical-school place; evaluate the bachelor's programme itself.

University of Notre Dame

Notre Dame merits consideration for business, economics, architecture and a residential university experience. Its Catholic identity also shapes campus life, so academic fit and personal fit belong in the same conversation.

Check your programme's structure and duration, particularly for architecture. Include any additional year in the budget.

University of Michigan, Ann Arbor

Michigan offers a broad public research setting, with options across engineering, business, the arts and social sciences. It suits students who want substantial subject choice alongside a large university community.

University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign

UIUC belongs on a Midwest shortlist for computing, engineering and business. Its admission data shows why an overall acceptance rate can mislead.

For 2025 first-year entry, Illinois reported a 36.6% overall admit rate, compared with 7.4% for computer science and 17.4% for Computer Science + X programmes. These different admission rates by route describe past applicant groups, not your personal chance of admission. Choose a programme because its content fits your interests, rather than treating another major as a guaranteed route into CS.

Purdue University, West Lafayette

Purdue is worth comparing for engineering, computer science and aviation-related study. Keep the campus clear: this profile concerns West Lafayette, and other Purdue locations can have different programme arrangements.

Budget by subject, too. The published international engineering and computing rate exceeds the general undergraduate rate, as the cost table below shows. A tuition-freeze headline cannot tell you everything about a particular student's bill. Review the relevant course fees and application priority dates together.

University of Wisconsin-Madison

Wisconsin-Madison offers a large research university in a state-capital setting. Students considering life sciences, engineering, economics or business can explore several academic directions within one institution.

Ask how undergraduates join research projects, whether your major has additional entry requirements and how easily you could change direction.

Case Western Reserve University

Case Western, in Cleveland, provides a useful comparison for biomedical engineering, nursing and science-based study. Students interested in healthcare should distinguish between a professional undergraduate course and a science degree that supports later applications.

Its 2026-27 first-year residential budget reaches $95,704 before variable transport costs. That makes a confirmed financial-aid offer central to the decision. Compare what your intended department offers undergraduates, then assess whether the net cost remains manageable throughout the degree.

Carleton College

Carleton, in Northfield, Minnesota, offers a smaller liberal arts environment. Consider it if you want to study sciences or humanities within a broad undergraduate curriculum rather than enter a large professional school immediately.

Small does not mean inexpensive. Carleton's published 2026-27 attendance budget is $97,870, with its health insurance charge listed separately. Evaluate the academic experience and your eventual aid package together; the college's size alone tells you little about affordability.

Grinnell College

Grinnell offers an alternative for students who want substantial freedom in choosing their studies. Its individually advised academic approach combines curriculum flexibility with faculty guidance and opportunities such as mentored advanced projects.

That freedom requires planning. Someone combining economics, statistics and environmental interests still needs the right prerequisites. Compare Grinnell with Chicago if curriculum structure matters to you.

Ohio State University, Columbus

Ohio State suits students seeking a large public university with choices across business, engineering, arts and health-related subjects. Columbus also offers a city setting rather than a small, self-contained college town.

Check which courses admit students directly and which involve later progression requirements. University admission and entry to your preferred major may involve different steps. Then examine department-level internship and graduate-destination information.

13 More Midwest Options to Consider

Use these additional Midwest colleges to test what your first shortlist may be missing:

  • City access: Minnesota Twin Cities, Macalester and Marquette offer different institution sizes in metropolitan settings.
  • Applied subjects: Iowa State, Michigan State, Kansas and Missouri S&T broaden the engineering, agriculture and professional-study comparison.
  • Business, music and writing: Indiana Bloomington, Iowa, Kenyon and St. Olaf offer contrasting routes, from large public universities to smaller liberal arts colleges.

Denison and DePauw add residential liberal arts alternatives. Compare their actual courses and campus settings with your favourites rather than adding applications simply to make the list longer.

Best Public and Private Universities in the Midwest

Best public research universities in the Midwest

Michigan, UIUC, Purdue, Wisconsin-Madison, Ohio State and Minnesota Twin Cities form a useful starting group for students seeking broad research-university options. Iowa State, Kansas and Missouri S&T expand the comparison, particularly for applied subjects.

Private universities in the Midwest

Chicago, Northwestern, WashU, Notre Dame and Case Western offer different combinations of curriculum, professional study and campus culture. Compare them by the undergraduate experience you want, not simply by reputation.

A private university with a higher published price can cost an eligible student less after grants than a public university with limited aid. The financial-aid offer determines whether that applies to you.

A mechanical engineering applicant and a computer engineering applicant need not arrive at the same shortlist.

Best Liberal Arts and Smaller Colleges in the Midwest

Among Midwest liberal arts colleges, Carleton, Grinnell, Macalester, Kenyon, Denison, St. Olaf and DePauw offer alternatives to large research universities. Consider them for broad study in an undergraduate-focused setting.

Liberal arts includes science and mathematics, not just literature and history. However, students seeking a named professional degree should confirm that the college actually offers it. A physics degree and a mechanical engineering degree prepare students differently.

For small or mid-size colleges, check current undergraduate enrolment and typical class formats. The word “university” in an institution's name does not reliably tell you how large your classes will feel.

One practical detail is easy to miss: arriving from a warm country means buying winter clothing as well as booking flights. Include those initial expenses, summer accommodation if needed, and the cost of suitable student health cover before judging affordability.

Scholarships and Financial Aid for International Students

Iowa State's competitive international merit awards include an Award of Achievement worth $5,000 to $10,000 annually, up to $40,000 in total, and an Award of Distinction worth $2,000 to $4,000 annually, up to $16,000. First-year applicants need the relevant OneApp application. Renewal requires conditions including a minimum 2.5 cumulative GPA and at least 12 credits per semester.

Northwestern takes a different approach. Its international undergraduate aid policy considers financial need during admission and meets demonstrated need for international aid recipients. Applicants must request and receive assistance in their first year to seek it later.

Choose your programme first, then confirm its available entry term. A January application deadline can lead to an autumn start; it does not necessarily mean January admission.

Purdue's first-year application schedule lists 1 November for Early Action and spring applications, and 15 January for Regular Decision. It also warns that some majors do not accept spring starters. The schedule presents recurring dates, so confirm the applicable 2027 term and programme availability in the application portal.

Prepare transcripts, required recommendations, application responses and any programme-specific materials. Check each institution's English-language and SAT/ACT policy separately; there is no single Midwest-wide requirement. Applicants already studying at university should also establish whether they must apply as transfers.

What Does “Regional Universities Midwest” Mean?

“Regional Universities Midwest” refers to a particular category in some college-ranking systems. It is not interchangeable with every university geographically located in the Midwest.

A broad regional comparison can include national research universities and liberal arts colleges that appear in different ranking tables. Always check the publisher, edition and category before comparing positions. A category winner and a nationally ranked research university have not necessarily competed against the same institutions.

How to Build Your Midwest College Shortlist

Start with your intended subject and identify programmes you would actually want to complete. Check admission requirements next, including any separate selection for the major.

Check outcomes through federal college comparison data and university reports. Compare graduation rate, first-year retention rate and earnings only after checking the cohort and reporting period. Graduate employment and further study measure different destinations; neither guarantees your own outcome.

Finally, compare everyday life: city or college town, housing, class format and travel. Those details can separate two otherwise similar choices.

Frequently Asked Questions

What are the best colleges in the Midwest?

Chicago, Northwestern, Michigan, WashU and Notre Dame are useful research-university starting points. Carleton and Grinnell offer smaller liberal arts alternatives. Your preferred major, learning environment and net cost should determine the final order.

Which Midwest universities should engineering students compare?

Begin with Michigan, UIUC and Purdue. Add Wisconsin-Madison, Minnesota Twin Cities, Iowa State or Missouri S&T according to your engineering branch, admission profile and budget. Compare programmes rather than university names alone.

Are there affordable universities in the Midwest for international students?

Yes, but affordability depends on your budget and confirmed aid. Iowa State and Purdue provide useful public-university cost comparisons here. Even their published international budgets exceed $50,000 before aid, with additional costs possible.

Can international students receive scholarships?

Some institutions offer merit scholarships or need-based assistance. Iowa State publishes competitive international merit awards; Northwestern offers need-based aid under its international admission policy. Eligibility, deadlines and renewal conditions differ.

Are any Ivy League universities in the Midwest?

No. The eight Ivy League universities are in the northeastern United States. Labels such as “Ivy of the Midwest” are informal comparisons, not membership or an official ranking category.

Can I start at a Midwest university in January 2027?

Some programmes accept spring entry, but availability varies by institution, major and applicant type. Verify the start term before applying. A January deadline may instead relate to Fall 2027 entry.

Conclusion: Choose Your Midwest University by Fit

The best universities in the Midwest offer different routes to a good undergraduate education. Start with Michigan, UIUC or Purdue for an engineering comparison; consider Chicago, Northwestern, WashU or Notre Dame for their particular academic options; and explore Carleton or Grinnell for a smaller liberal arts setting.
